US-518 DONE (Sprint 69 / V0.29.24, 9/11). Sync-success re-anchor of the derived altitude to pi.location.home.elevationM. Commit cf977ac.

THE ONE THE NEXT AGENT AND THE PM MUST KNOW: THERE IS NO DERIVED-ALTITUDE ACCUMULATOR IN THE CODEBASE. US-518's AC says 'reset the derived altitude accumulator', but the thing that would produce it is US-519, DEFERRED this sprint pending Spool's sigma on US-521; states/imu.altitude is a typed NULL with reason no_source (no barometer on the ICM-20948). I built the accumulator + the reset and left the INTEGRATION to US-519. Did not file a blocker: the AC itself says 'small utility on the sync-success seam', and WP-2/US-517 landed the same way (read path, no consumer yet). But do not read the story as having wired something that already existed.

THE LINE I HELD, and it is why this is not a 20-line story: the anchor publishes NOTHING. If it fed states/imu, the panel would render home-elevation-forever as the altitude the moment the car left the driveway -- a confident wrong number, worse than the honest 'no source' shown today and against the sprint's own keyReminder. Internal state only. US-520 wires the display once US-519 makes the value mean something.

SEAM: hooked CardStateEmitterMixin._recordSyncOutcome, NOT the two call sites in core.py. It is the single point both sync paths converge on and is reached only past the US-340 offline route gate, so 'sync succeeded' and 'we are on the home network' are the same fact there. One hook = a future third sync path cannot silently skip it (the US-512 'missing call site (b)' shape). Two things I verified rather than assumed: it is NOT gated by pi.dashboard.stateEmitEnabled (only emitter CONSTRUCTION is), so drift control does not ride a display flag; and the powerwatch forcePush is a SEPARATE PROCESS with no in-memory accumulator, so it is deliberately not wired -- do not 'fix' that omission.

THE REAL RISK IS NOT A FAILED PUSH, IT IS THE ROUTE GATE. Mid-drive, miles from home, the US-340 gate bails before pushing; re-anchoring there resets altitude to home elevation while the car is nowhere near home. That is the fabrication this WP exists to prevent, and it is the negative test that matters most. Note 'partial' resolves as FIRES: a push that reaches the server with some tables failing still proves we are on the home network, as does a zero-row push -- the trigger is 'we are home', not 'we had data'. Defensible either way; stated so the PM can NAK it cheaply.

NO-OP ON THE PI TODAY (inherited from US-517, restated because it bounds validation): deploy-pi.sh excludes .env, so PI_HOME_ELEVATION_M is unresolved on the box and the re-anchor correctly does nothing until the CIO writes that line into the Pi's .env. The story's validationCriteria is simulation-based and IS satisfied by the real-chain test -- but that is not live-validated on the Pi.

47 tests. All RED first, but honestly: the module did not exist, so run 1 was one ModuleNotFoundError, not 47 witnessed assertion failures. 3 mutations proved -- drop the hook -> 7 red incl. end-to-end; fabricate sea level on an unknown anchor -> 8 red; disable the isfinite guard -> 3 red. Boot-order trap avoided for the SIXTH time this sprint (home elevation read lazily per re-anchor, so a Pi whose .env gains the value later starts working with no code change).

Green in-loop: tests/pi/location + tests/pi/orchestrator + tests/pi/splash = exit 0, 363 tests, 1 skip, with 2 deselected (below); ruff clean on all 4 files. architecture.md section 6 updated in-sprint (design-gate DoD).

PRE-EXISTING FAILURE, NOT MINE -- I-041 FILED: tests/pi/splash/test_system_status_emitter.py has 2 red tests. US-505 (65de58d) added drive.lastDrive to buildSystemStatusState but never updated that file (last touched f929ed8/US-480-a); both assert the EXACT state shape, so the new key breaks them -- the guard working. Provenance checked via git log per file, not assumed. ~2-line fix, outside my fence. IT WILL FAIL THE PM INTEGRATION GATE, and it is the SECOND red on this branch after TD-073. Both were invisible to the story that caused them because the scoped in-loop selection did not include the EXISTING guards for the contract being changed -- worth asking whether TD-059's in-loop/PM-gate split needs a middle tier.
